surfaces.name: telemetry
surfaces.what: telemetry.unbrowse.ai: POST /v1/events from nodes, POST /v1/reports (bug reports to GitHub issues), GET /v1/stats/<name> for the team, and the TelemetryStore Durable Object behind them
unit: telemetry worker tests, on the D1-shaped stand-in and through the Durable Object client
e2e: deployed telemetry worker: keeps a node's batch, refuses bad ones, stats door needs the token

waive.user: Its only users are nodes, and a node sends only once it is on the network, so a throwaway node can't be a reliable gate. The production watch an hour on stands in: it needs real release nodes' installs in the counts.

surfaces.name: rpc
surfaces.what: rpc.unbrowse.ai: POST /members from the link page (a Privy access token and a node), POST /<network>/<pass> JSON-RPC from member nodes relayed to Alchemy, and the Members Durable Object behind them
unit: rpc gateway tests: node passes, Privy tokens, the methods and log ranges it relays
e2e: deployed rpc gateway: answers, refuses a membership without a Privy token, a non-member's pass and a pass for another network

waive.user: A member's path needs a real Privy sign-in, which a gate can't make. It was run by hand against a deployed copy on 18 November 2026 (PR evidence); the node's own use, once it ships, is the standing check.

surfaces.name: dashboard
surfaces.what: The test dashboard (UNB-250): the page at / with its charts and runs table, GET /api/runs and /api/sites, GET /healthz, and POST /api/ingest that CI signs with DASHBOARD_INGEST_KEY (dashboard-post.yml); D1 behind them
unit: dashboard tests: artifact parsers, signing, the ingest and read doors on SQLite with the real migrations
e2e: deployed dashboard: refuses unsigned, wrongly signed, stale and malformed posts, keeps a signed run, and a browser reads it off the page at phone and desktop width

waive.user: A read-only page: a simulated person reading it changes nothing a command could check, and the train's rules never take the agent's word as proof. Stand-in: the e2e gate drives the deployed page in a real browser at phone and desktop width and reads a made-up run's number off it; CI's own posts are its other user, measured by run id in the PR.
